what: ADDITION 2 — switch_branch (OA2) coordinate census on gen-16's bait states
method: contrib = mean|value| x ||W_col||, captured by a forward hook on switch_branch.proj's INPUT (the [B,4,9] raw stack). Coordinate names from SWITCH_BRANCH_COORDS, never re-spelled.

populations.note: the bait-conditioned sets built from the loops census; ranking is identical across both

FINDING: e_mult_switch — the coordinate that literally encodes 'your move does ~0x into the arrival' — carries the SECOND-HIGHEST raw signal (mean|v| 0.6416) on the EIGHTH-largest weight (||W|| 0.1132). Its column norm is 8.1x smaller than wasted_ko's. a_switch is worse: highest signal of all nine (0.7514) on the smallest weight of all nine (0.0549). The DERIVED anti-bait product (wasted_ko = pko_stay . alpha_SWITCH) took 55% of the learned mass while the RAW PHYSICS coordinate that encodes the immunity got 20%.
why_it_matters: All 79 gen-16 whiffs were kind=immune (not fail, not near_zero), so e_mult_switch is THE coordinate for this bait class. This is c1's lesson repeating on a new block: a constant/derived indicator out-delivering the real physics.
SECOND_CONTENT_GAP: e_pko_switch is annotated 'NULLED at hidden' in the source and reads mean|v| 0.048, near-dead. It is nulled exactly when the arrival is unrevealed — which is exactly the bait case. The P(KO)-into-arrival coordinate is switched off precisely where the fact would be worth having.
CONSEQUENCE: The insufficiency is NOT purely credit-assignment; part of it is CONTENT-MIX, fixable by construction. That matters because the training-pressure lever (TD-aux) was falsified on its own pre-registered direction the same night — so a content-mix fix is the live option, not the fallback.
candidate_fixes_increasing_intrusiveness: rescale/normalise the raw coordinates before the projection so a high-variance column cannot be learned down
give immunity its OWN coordinate instead of burying it in an expectation over arrivals
un-null e_pko_switch at hidden, or supply a belief-weighted substitute
CAVEATS: mean|v| x ||W_col|| is a FIRST-ORDER PROXY, not a causal ablation: it ranks columns by linear influence at the projection and does NOT prove that up-weighting e_mult_switch moves the policy. The proving experiment is a per-coordinate zero-and-remeasure, NOT RUN.
n = 23 loop / 79 whiff states. The RANKING is stable across both populations; the shares to one decimal are not.
||W_col|| is measured on the TRAINED model, so 'underweighted' means the network learned to down-weight it — which is itself the finding, not a claim that the init was wrong.
